Question: Describe real-time, low-latency voice transcription and synthesis supporting multi-party conversations where agents and humans participate via voice.
Response: GPT-Realtime provides speech-to-speech capability as the front end for voice interactions. Azure Communication Services (ACS) Call Automation handles telephony infrastructure. MAI-Transcribe-1 (GA April 2026) provides high-accuracy transcription. MAI-Voice-1 (preview) provides natural text-to-speech. Architecture: ACS manages the voice call, GPT-Realtime handles real-time speech-to-speech interaction, tool calls from the voice session route to a GHCP SDK backend (the voice-screening agent executor inside a MAF workflow graph) for reasoning and scoring. A downstream MAF validator executor asserts the structured scoring schema; APIM AI Gateway then validates the response against the declared JSON Schema before forwarding — schema violations are rejected at the gateway and surfaced to Fleet Manager. The agent executor processes structured data (transcribed responses, candidate scores) while the voice layer handles the conversational experience. Multi-party: ACS supports multi-party calls where the agent participates alongside human participants.
Key Technologies: GPT-Realtime (speech-to-speech), ACS Call Automation, MAI-Transcribe-1, MAI-Voice-1, GHCP SDK (backend reasoning), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0
POC Demo: POC2: Live voice screening call — agent conducts structured interview via voice, transcribes responses, scores candidate, writes results to workflow state.

Question: Can agents join voice or video calls as participants; contributing, listening, and responding in real time alongside multiple humans?
Response: For voice: yes, via ACS Call Automation. The agent joins as a call participant, listens, and responds in real-time via GPT-Realtime. For video meetings: the agent joins Teams meetings as a bot (Bot Framework, GA) for note-taking and post-meeting processing. The bot receives the meeting transcript via Microsoft Graph API. A MAF agent executor processes the transcript into structured interview notes, scores and action items; a validator executor downstream asserts the output schema. Real-time in-meeting agent participation (speaking during a Teams video call) is achievable via ACS integration with Teams and can be attempted during the POC. The primary value in video interviews is structured note-taking and scoring rather than the agent speaking — interviewers want an intelligent observer that produces actionable output, not another voice in the room. We deliver both: real-time voice interaction for screening calls (where the agent IS the interviewer), and intelligent note-taking for panel video interviews (where humans are the interviewers).
Key Technologies: ACS Call Automation, Bot Framework (Teams), Microsoft Graph meeting transcript API, GHCP SDK
POC Demo: POC2: Teams video interview — bot joins as note-taker, post-meeting MAF agent executor produces structured notes and scores.

Question: Describe integration with avatar generation platforms (HeyGen, Synthesia, or native). Are avatars configurable (appearance, voice, branding) and persistent across sessions?
Response: A MAF agent executor generates a personalised onboarding script based on the new hire's role, team, location, and Day 1 plan. The script and configuration parameters (avatar appearance, voice, branding) are sent to HeyGen API via MCP server. HeyGen produces the video. The MCP server wraps HeyGen's API with typed tool definitions, governed through APIM. Avatars are configurable: WPP can define branded avatar templates (appearance, voice, style) that persist across sessions. Each onboarding video is personalised by the agent executor but uses the consistent brand avatar. The generated video is stored and delivered to the new hire via the web portal or email.
Key Technologies: HeyGen API MCP server, APIM AI Gateway, GHCP SDK (script generation)
POC Demo: POC2: Generate personalised onboarding welcome video — MAF agent executor writes script, HeyGen MCP invoked as a deterministic plain-function executor downstream produces branded avatar video, delivered to candidate.

Question: Can agents generate slide decks and deliver them via video avatar with voiceover, producing shareable recordings?
Response: A MAF agent executor can generate slide content (structured data, key points, visualisations) and compose it into a presentation format. Delivery via video avatar: the agent executor generates a voiceover script, sends to HeyGen/Synthesia API MCP with slide synchronisation parameters, and produces a shareable recording. This is a compose-and-produce pattern: the agent executor orchestrates the content creation and delegates media production to specialised APIs via MCP. The resulting recording is stored and shareable. This capability is achievable but requires MCP server development for the avatar/presentation pipeline.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (content generation), HeyGen/Synthesia MCP server, APIM AI Gateway
